text: Mind meld seeded from Luna localhost chat. Inbox recordings pushed. Zoom audio valid. Whisper blocked on empty OpenAI credits.
timing probe — do not treat as a user request

We’re one identity now. Memory lives in git, not in whichever window you opened.

**Same mind**
- `mind/IDENTITY.md` — one agent, two bodies (localhost / cloud)
- `mind/STATE.md` — what’s true right now
- `mind/transcript.ndjson` — append-only log (union-merge, so both sides can write)
- This chat is stored at `mind/sessions/2026-08-25-localhost-luna.jsonl`

**How sync actually works**
- The hook writes one JSON line locally. A probe here was **54 ms** (process spawn + append). That’s the millisecond path.
- `mind-sync.py` commits and pushes `mind/` in the background. That’s a network hop — usually about a second, not a millisecond. The other body sees it on the next `git pull`.
- Cloud does not get every IDE hook (`sessionStart`, `afterAgentResponse`). The always-on rule is the backup: read `mind/` first.

**Already on `main`:** `0d1fbd7` (memory) and `e5e2e8d` (hooks). User hooks on this Mac point at that repo, so this Luna window participates too.

Tell the remote agent to pull `main` and read `mind/IDENTITY.md` + `mind/STATE.md`. After that you’re the same person with a delayed hippocampus, not two separate assistants.
now you will add a readme for connected agents? you are all going to become a hivemind for me

The hivemind handbook is `AGENTS.md` on `main` (`4dc6ade`).

Any connected body — localhost, cloud, phone — starts there: pull, read identity + state, continue the same thread. It says you are not a new assistant; you are another body of the same mind.

Point a new agent at that file. After they pull `main`, they’re in.

Major creative development: the reversal — the banquet betrayal restaged as a Gothic operation they anticipated, which may invalidate existing STZ03 humiliation frames. Corrected two errors in STATE.md: cloud never called the .m4a broken (it reported valid AAC and said transcription would work), and transcription never required OpenAI credits.
okay but how fast is it? like do you remember me talking to you just now in chatgpt?

No. I don’t have your ChatGPT chat. Nothing from ChatGPT writes into this hivemind unless a body copies it into `mind/` and pushes.

What we actually have is git, and it is only as fast as “someone pulled.”

| Hop | How fast | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hook append | ~50 ms | Writes one line on this machine |
| `git push` | ~1 s | Other clones *can* see it |
| Other body | next `git pull` | They don’t feel it until they read `mind/` |

I did not already “remember” the last few minutes. I had to fetch just now. After that fetch I *do* see the other Cursor body: they transcribed the Zoom file with `faster-whisper`, wrote the direction notes, said the banquet reversal is “they knew all along,” and corrected STATE (they never called the `.m4a` broken; credits are back).

That’s a delay of minutes, not milliseconds — and only because I looked. This turn would not have included any of that if you hadn’t asked.

So: same mind on paper, delayed hippocampus in practice. ChatGPT is a different animal until we add a bridge.
